packageAssets: Shared-framework Components and Server/JSInterop; SDK-resolved Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Internal.Assets 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105 supplies static framework assets.
providers: ASP.NET Core Data Protection; ephemeral in-memory keys for this disposable sample only.
platforms: Portable managed server/renderer; executed on Windows x64. No native SDK or optional workload.
renderingModes: Real Interactive Server circuits after activation, same-origin JavaScript and server-side DI ProtectedSessionStorage; no prerender interop, WASM client, full circuit protocol or NativeAOT support.
prerequisites: Use all files below as one project per release, including wwwroot when present. The .NET 10 comparison remains valid; no new API route on net10.0 is claimed.
constraints: Cedar Planetarium sends ShowTicket through both real paths. TicketJson supplies generated metadata only for that record; ExtraNote deliberately falls through both resolvers to reflection. The first registered resolver wins; the second throws if asked to own ShowTicket.

Use injected ProtectedSessionStorage/ProtectedLocalStorage from framework DI. Manually constructing a storage instance does not use the configured resolver chain. Configure once at startup, before options are cached; do not put per-user mutable state in resolvers.

Resolvers return null for unhandled types. Preserve framework converters and reflection fallback. The sample passes a real ElementReference alongside each JS payload as a converter control; generated metadata does not make all framework messages source generated.

Protected session storage is server-side Data Protection over per-tab browser session storage. It is not authorization, a cross-tab/session data service or a guarantee against deletion/replay. Browser access is unavailable during prerender.

Ephemeral keys keep the demo disposable and create no persistent key ring. Restarting the host loses decryption ability. A production server needs its own reviewed persistent key lifecycle; this recipe does not deploy one.

The bounded trace observes options identities and type names, caps history at 64 entries and retains no payloads. It is test instrumentation. Distinct options/circuit state does not promise that configured resolver instances are per-circuit. Concurrent resolvers must be safe for shared use.
Server-side Blazor does not currently support trimming or NativeAOT. This is not a circuit-protocol, AOT, zero-reflection, external-provider or production-security qualification.
optIns: Local #pragma warning disable/restore ASPNETCORE9004 around JsonTypeInfoResolvers registrations. The API is experimental and EditorBrowsable(Never); no project-wide suppression.
stabilityLimitations: Experimental API; compatibility can change. Actual evidence: SDK 10.0.402 / runtime 10.0.13 and SDK 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105 / runtime 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105. GA reconciliation and comprehensive publication remain open.

sources.title: DI storage construction and trimming limitation

evidence.scope: Record-CedarPayload.ps1 captures exact compilation inputs/dependencies, then Test-CedarPayload.mjs runs both real local servers in Chromium with two separate circuits/tabs each. ShowTicket and ExtraNote round-trip over JS interop and DI protected session storage. Trace assertions distinguish four independent serializer options instances in RC2, preserve registration order and exercise reflection fallback; each app retains its own scope values and stored ticket. Ciphertext conceals the payload and an altered ciphertext is rejected by real Data Protection. Compile-only evidence is separate from saved execution records. These checks do not claim exhaustive security or production key management.
